title: Knowledge check: Denial of Service and Gas-Limit Risks

questions.prompt: Which statement best demonstrates understanding of Denial of Service and Gas-Limit Risks?
options: It guarantees that every contract using the concept is secure.
It removes the need to check compiler output or runtime behavior.
It means denial of service and gas-limit risks should be understood through its role in Solidity behavior, with assumptions and limits made explicit.
It should be used without testing because the EVM is deterministic.
questions.answer_key: It means denial of service and gas-limit risks should be understood through its role in Solidity behavior, with assumptions and limits made explicit.
questions.explanation: The lesson treats Denial of Service and Gas-Limit Risks as a technical concept whose meaning depends on execution context and explicit assumptions. It does not guarantee security or replace testing.

questions.prompt: What is the best practice when applying Denial of Service and Gas-Limit Risks in a new contract?
options: Build a minimal example about Denial of Service and Gas-Limit Risks, predict its outcome, and verify normal and edge cases in a controlled local environment.
Skip negative tests once one happy-path call succeeds.
Rely only on comments instead of checking behavior.
Start on mainnet so gas reports reflect real funds.
questions.answer_key: Build a minimal example about Denial of Service and Gas-Limit Risks, predict its outcome, and verify normal and edge cases in a controlled local environment.
questions.explanation: Small, repeatable local tests make assumptions visible while avoiding unnecessary exposure. Failure cases are important because success-only tests leave many requirements unchecked.

questions.prompt: Before relying on Denial of Service and Gas-Limit Risks in a release, what should a reviewer do?
options: Treat code that compiles as proof that it cannot fail.
Check the versioned official guidance, inspect compiler/test evidence, and document limitations before relying on the behavior.
Assume documentation examples work with every compiler and EVM version.
Remove safeguards if they make a test more difficult.
questions.answer_key: Check the versioned official guidance, inspect compiler/test evidence, and document limitations before relying on the behavior.
questions.explanation: Compiler and network capabilities change, and a compiling example can still have logic or security defects. Versioned sources, reproducible tests, and honest limitations support a responsible review.
